items.title: Helical selected for Japanese fusion demonstration project
items.summary: Tokyo-based fusion company Helical Fusion announced it has been conditionally selected by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry for a project aimed at demonstrating fusion energy power generation in the 2030s.

items.title: Blykalla seeks state aid for second SMR plant
items.summary: Sweden's Blykalla has applied for state support for its proposed small modular reactor power plant at Untra in the Tierp municipality, for which the company applied for governmental approval last week.

items.title: Decommissioning of Chernobyl units progressing
items.summary: Preparatory work for the next phase of decommissioning the three intact reactor units at Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant is due to be completed by the end of 2028, the operators of the site say.

items.title: India and Uzbekistan eye uranium deal as ties grow
items.summary: The leaders of India and Uzbekistan have announced plans to increase bilateral trade to USD5 billion per year. A long-term uranium supply arrangement looks likely to be part of that.

items.title: Tennessee issues licence for fusion plant
items.summary: The Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation has issued the state's first fusion-specific byproduct material licence to Type One Energy in preparation for its commercial fusion project. Tennessee is the first US state to issue a licence under a new regulatory framework specifically for nuclear fusion machines.

items.title: IAEA concern over diesel supply for Zaporizhzhia generators
items.summary: The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant has been relying on emergency diesel generators for more than 11 days, with the International Atomic Energy Agency raising concerns about fuel supplies if the loss of external power continues.
